questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Suppose $A$ is denoted the set of all numbers between 1 and 700 which are divisible by 3 and let $B$ is denoted the set of all numbers between 1 and 300 which are divisible by 7. If $C = \{(a, b) | a \in A, b \in B, a \neq b \text{ and } a + b = \text{even number}\}$, then order of $C$ is
questions.solution:
The set $A$ contains multiples of $3$ from $1$ to $700$.
Number of elements in $A = \lfloor \dfrac{700}{3} \rfloor = 233$.
Number of even elements in $A = \lfloor \dfrac{700}{6} \rfloor = 116$.
Number of odd elements in $A = 233 - 116 = 117$.

The set $B$ contains multiples of $7$ from $1$ to $300$.
Number of elements in $B = \lfloor \dfrac{300}{7} \rfloor = 42$.
Number of even elements in $B = \lfloor \dfrac{300}{14} \rfloor = 21$.
Number of odd elements in $B = 42 - 21 = 21$.

For the sum $a + b$ to be even, both $a$ and $b$ must be even, or both must be odd.
Total number of such pairs $(a, b)$ is $(116 \times 21) + (117 \times 21) = 2436 + 2457 = 4893$.

The condition $a \neq b$ requires subtracting pairs where $a = b$.
If $a = b$, then $a$ is a multiple of both $3$ and $7$, which means $a$ is a multiple of $21$.
Since $b \in B$, we have $b \le 300$, so $a = b \le 300$.
Number of such pairs is $\lfloor \dfrac{300}{21} \rfloor = 14$.
Since $a = b$ makes $a + b = 2a$ which is even, these $14$ pairs are included in the $4893$ pairs.

The order of $C$ is $4893 - 14 = 4879$.

Answer: 4879

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $a, b$ and $c$ are positive numbers in a GP, then the roots of the quadratic equation $\left(\log _{e} a\right) x^{2}-\left(2 \log _{e} b\right) x+\left(\log _{e} c\right)=0$ are
questions.solution:
Since, $a, b$ and $c$ are in $\mathrm{GP}$.
$\therefore b^{2}=a c$
Given equation is
$(\log _{e} \text { a) } x^{2}-\left(2 \log _{e} \text { b) } x+\log _{e} c\right)=0$
Put $x=1,$ we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \log _{e} a-2 \log _{e} b+\log _{e} c=0 \\
\Rightarrow & 2 \log _{e} b=\log _{e} a+\log _{0} c \\
\Rightarrow \quad & \log _{e} b^{2}=\log _{e} a c
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad b^{2}=a c,$ which is true.
Hence, one of the root of given equation is $1 .$
Let another root be $\alpha$.
$\therefore$ Sum of roots, $1+\alpha=\frac{2 \log _{e} b}{\log _{e} a}=\frac{\log _{e} b^{2}}{\log _{e} a}\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \quad a &=\frac{\log _{e} a c}{\log _{e} a}-1 \\
&=\frac{\left(\log _{e} a+\log _{e} c\right)}{\log _{e} a}-1 \\
&=\frac{\log _{e} c}{\log _{c} a}=\log _{a} c
\end{aligned}$
Hence, roots are 1 and $\log _{a} c .$

questions.q: The number of solutions of the equation $\frac{1}{2} \log _{\sqrt{3}}\left(\frac{x+1}{x+5}\right)+\log _{9}(x+5)^{2}=1$ is
questions.solution:
Given equation is $\frac{1}{2} \log _{\sqrt{3}}\left(\frac{x+1}{x+5}\right)+\log _{9}(x+5)^{2}=1\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{2} \cdot\left(\frac{1}{1 / 2}\right) \log _{3}\left(\frac{x+1}{x+5}\right)+\frac{1}{2} \log _{3}(x+5)^{2}=1\left(\because \log _{a^{n}} b=\frac{1}{n} \log _{a} b\right)\Rightarrow \quad \frac{2}{2} \log _{3}\left(\frac{x+1}{x+5}\right)+\frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \log _{3}(x+5)=\log _{3} 3\Rightarrow \quad \log _{3}\left\{\left(\frac{x+1}{x+5} \cdot(x+5)\right)\right\}=\log _{3} 3\left(\because \log m+\log n=\log m n\right.$ and $\log _{n} n=1\Rightarrow \quad(x+1)=3 \Rightarrow x=2$
So, only one solution is possible.

questions.q:
If $x=1+\frac{1}{2 \times 1 !}+\frac{1}{4 \times 2 !}+\frac{1}{8 \times 3 !}+\ldots$ and
$y=1+\frac{x^{2}}{1 !}+\frac{x^{4}}{2 !}+\frac{x^{6}}{3 !}+\ldots$
Then, the value of loge $y$ is
questions.solution:
Given,
$x=1+\frac{1}{2 \times 1 !}+\frac{1}{4 \times 2 !}+\frac{1}{8 \times 3 !}+\ldots\Rightarrow \quad x=1+\frac{(1 / 2)^{\prime}}{1 !}+\frac{(1 / 2)^{2}}{2 !}+\frac{(1 / 2)^{3}}{3 !}+\ldots\Rightarrow \quad x=e^{1 / 2} \Rightarrow x^{2}=e$
and $\quad y=1+\frac{x^{2}}{1 !}+\frac{x^{4}}{2 !}+\frac{x^{6}}{3 !}+\ldots\Rightarrow \quad y=1+\frac{\left(x^{2}\right)^{1}}{1 !}+\frac{\left(x^{2}\right)^{2}}{2 !}+\frac{\left(x^{2}\right)^{3}}{3 !}+\ldots\Rightarrow \quad y=e^{x^{2}}=e^{e} \quad$ [from Eq. (i)]
Taking log on both sides, we get
log$y=e$

Since, $x=1$ and $x=-3$ are satisfy the given equation therefore the number of solutions of the equation are two.
